factors.name: Choice-dominated branching vs. mixed, dense connectors
factors.summary: All four retained measures load strongly on this single factor, with mixed signs. Connector Heterogeneity (-0.995), Density (-0.886) and Token split (-0.773) fall as the factor rises, while Control flow complexity (+0.723) increases. High scores therefore describe sparse nets with many choice-split arcs, few parallel splits and connectors mostly of one type, and low scores describe denser nets that mix parallel and choice connectors.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO of 0.72 exceeds the 0.6 threshold, so the retained data are suitable for factor analysis. Only one eigenvalue exceeds 1 (3.14, then 0.59), and the single unrotated factor explains 72% of the variance of the four measures. Because only one factor was extracted, it is necessarily a general factor over the retained measures. Its mixed-sign loadings contrast choice-based branching in sparse nets with heterogeneous, parallel-rich and denser nets. The MSA filter removed eight of the twelve measures, including Size, so the result describes a narrow subset of model complexity.
caveats: Eight measures, including Size, Sequentiality and Separability, were removed by the MSA filter, so the factor covers only four measures and says nothing about the dimensions the removed measures represent.
Bartlett's df of 66 corresponds to twelve measures, which suggests the test was computed before MSA filtering rather than on the four retained measures.
Connector Heterogeneity has a communality of 0.99, close to a Heywood case, so the factor is almost identical to this one measure.
Connector Heterogeneity is undefined for nets without connectors, and how such nets were handled is not reported.
The choice-versus-parallelism reading is an inference from the signs of the loadings in this dataset of 288 discovered nets, not a causal finding.
